what_its_for: Lapatinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a certain type of breast cancer called HER2-positive breast cancer. It works by blocking signals inside cancer cells that tell them to grow and multiply. It is usually given together with another medicine called capecitabine (Xeloda) or letrozole (Femara).
how_to_take: Take lapatinib by mouth once a day, at the same time each day. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, cut, or chew them. Take this medicine on an EMPTY STOMACH, meaning at least 1 hour before eating or at least 1 hour after eating. Food — especially a high-fat meal — can cause too much of the medicine to enter your body at once, which can increase side effects. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep the medicine working steadily in your body.
dosing: The usual dose is 5 tablets (1250 mg) taken once a day when used with capecitabine, or 6 tablets (1500 mg) taken once a day when used with letrozole. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have side effects or other health conditions. Always take exactly the number of tablets your doctor prescribed — do not take more or less without asking your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time the following day. Do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. Double-dosing can cause serious side effects. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store lapatinib tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Store them away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets. If you have leftover or expired tablets, ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of them.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking lapatinib — it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid taking this medicine with food, especially high-fat meals. Avoid starting new medicines — including vitamins, supplements, and herbal products — without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, because many medicines can interact with lapatinib. St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) can make lapatinib less effective and should be avoided. Avoid driving or using machines if you feel dizzy or very tired.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, or a fast or irregular heartbeat (these could be signs of a serious heart problem); severe diarrhea that is not controlled with over-the-counter medicines; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or severe stomach pain; severe rash or blistering of the skin; swelling of the hands, feet, or ankles; trouble breathing or a new or worsening cough; high fever or signs of infection; or severe tiredness or weakness. Also call your doctor if you notice any new or unusual symptoms, or if your side effects are not going away.
when_it_works: Lapatinib does not cure cancer, but it works to slow or stop the growth of cancer cells. It may take several weeks before your doctor can tell whether the medicine is working for you. Your doctor will order regular tests (such as scans and blood work) to monitor how well the treatment is working. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own, even if you feel fine — talk to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Lapatinib can harm an unborn baby. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant. Women who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking lapatinib and for at least 1 week after your last dose. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially diarrhea and fatigue. Children: Lapatinib is not approved for use in children.
